verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要向以色列家出谜语，设比喻，
verses.en: “Son of man, offer a riddle[NOTE:1] and tell a parable to the house of Israel.
notes: The verb occurs elsewhere in the OT only in Judg 14:12-19, where Samson supplies a riddle.

verses.zh: 说主耶和华如此说：有一大鹰，翅膀大，翎毛长，羽毛丰满，彩色俱备，来到黎巴嫩，将香柏树梢拧去，
verses.en: Say to them: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:[NOTE:1] “‘A great eagle[NOTE:2] with broad wings, long feathers,[NOTE:3] with full plumage that was multihued,[NOTE:4] came to Lebanon[NOTE:5] and took the top of the cedar.
notes: The parable assumes the defection of Zedekiah to Egypt and his rejection of Babylonian lordship.
The great eagle symbolizes Nebuchadnezzar (17:12).

Hebrew has two words for wings; it is unknown whether they are fully synonymous or whether one term distinguishes a particular part of the wing such as the wing coverts (nearest the shoulder), secondaries (mid-feathers of the wing), or primaries (last and longest section of the wing).
This term was used in 16:10, 13, and 18 of embroidered cloth.
In the parable Lebanon apparently refers to Jerusalem (17:12).

verses.zh: 就是折去香柏树尽尖的嫩枝，叼到贸易之地，放在买卖城中；
verses.en: He plucked off its topmost shoot;he brought it to a land of merchantsand planted it in a city of traders.

verses.zh: 又将以色列地的枝子栽于肥田里，插在大水旁，如插柳树，
verses.en: He took one of the seedlings[NOTE:1] of the land, placed it in a cultivated plot;[NOTE:2] a shoot by abundant water,like a willow he planted it.
notes: Heb “took of the seed of the land.” For the vine imagery, “seedling” is a better translation, though in its subsequent interpretation the “seed” refers to Zedekiah through its common application to offspring.
Heb “a field for seed.”

verses.zh: 就渐渐生长，成为蔓延矮小的葡萄树。其枝转向那鹰，其根在鹰以下，于是成了葡萄树，生出枝子，发出小枝。
verses.en: It sprouted and became a vine,spreading low to the ground;[NOTE:1] its branches turning toward him,[NOTE:2] its roots were under itself.[NOTE:3] So it became a vine; it produced shoots and sent out branches.
notes: Heb “short of stature.”
That is, the eagle.
Or “him,” i.e., the eagle.

verses.zh: 又有一大鹰，翅膀大，羽毛多。这葡萄树从栽种的畦中向这鹰弯过根来，发出枝子，好得它的浇灌。
verses.en: “‘There was another great eagle[NOTE:1] with broad wings and thick plumage. Now this vine twisted its roots toward him and sent its branches toward himto be watered from the soil where it was planted.
notes: The phrase another great eagle refers to Pharaoh Hophra.

verses.zh: 这树栽于肥田多水的旁边，好生枝子，结果子，成为佳美的葡萄树。
verses.en: In a good field, by abundant waters, it was planted to grow branches, bear fruit, and become a beautiful vine.’

verses.zh: 你要说，主耶和华如此说：这葡萄树岂能发旺呢？鹰岂不拔出它的根来，芟除它的果子，使它枯干，使它发的嫩叶都枯干了吗？也不用大力和多民，就拔出它的根来。
verses.en: “Say to them: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: “‘Will it prosper? Will he not rip out its rootsand cause its fruit to rot[NOTE:1] and wither?All its foliage[NOTE:2] will wither. No strong arm or large armywill be needed to pull it out by its roots.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew root occurs only here in the OT and appears to have the meaning of “strip off.” In application to fruit the meaning may be “cause to rot.”
Heb “all the טַרְפֵּי (tarpe) of branches.” The word טַרְפֵּי occurs only here in the Bible; its precise meaning is uncertain.
Or “there will be no strong arm or large army when it is pulled up by the roots.”

verses.zh: 葡萄树虽然栽种，岂能发旺呢？一经东风，岂不全然枯干吗？必在生长的畦中枯干了。」
verses.en: Consider! It is planted, but will it prosper? Will it not wither completely when the east wind blows on it? Will it not wither in the soil where it sprouted?’”

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: Then the Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「你对那悖逆之家说：你们不知道这些事是甚么意思么？你要告诉他们说，巴比伦王曾到耶路撒冷，将其中的君王和首领带到巴比伦自己那里去。
verses.en: “Say to the rebellious house of Israel:[NOTE:1] ‘Don’t you know what these things mean?’[NOTE:2] Say: ‘See here, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem[NOTE:3] and took her king and her officials prisoner and brought them to himself in Babylon.
notes: The book of Ezekiel frequently refers to the Israelites as a rebellious house (Ezek 2:5, 6, 8; 3:9, 26-27; 12:2-3, 9, 25; 17:12; 24:3). tn The words “of Israel” are not in the Hebrew text but are supplied in the translation as a clarification of the referent.
The narrative description of this interpretation of the riddle is given in 2 Kgs 24:11-15.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 从以色列的宗室中取一人与他立约，使他发誓，并将国中有势力的人掳去，
verses.en: He took one from the royal family,[NOTE:1] made a treaty with him, and put him under oath.[NOTE:2] He then took the leaders of the land
notes: Or “descendants”; Heb “seed” (cf. v. 5).
Heb “caused him to enter into an oath.”

verses.zh: 使国低微不能自强，惟因守盟约得以存立。
verses.en: so it would be a lowly kingdom that could not rise on its own but had to keep its treaty with him in order to stand.

verses.zh: 他却背叛巴比伦王，打发使者往埃及去，要他们给他马匹和多民。他岂能亨通呢？行这样事的人岂能逃脱呢？他背约岂能逃脱呢？
verses.en: But this one from Israel’s royal family[NOTE:1] rebelled against the king of Babylon[NOTE:2] by sending his emissaries to Egypt to obtain horses and a large army. Will he prosper? Will the one doing these things escape? Can he break the covenant and escape?
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the member of the royal family, v. 13) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “him”; the referent (the king of Babylon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他轻看向王所起的誓，背弃王与他所立的约。主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，他定要死在立他作王、巴比伦王的京都。
verses.en: “‘As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, surely in the city[NOTE:1] of the king who crowned him, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke—in the middle of Babylon he will die!
notes: Heb “place.”

verses.zh: 敌人筑垒造台，与他打仗的时候，为要剪除多人，法老虽领大军队和大群众，还是不能帮助他。
verses.en: Pharaoh with his great army and mighty horde will not help[NOTE:1] him in battle, when siege ramps are erected and siege walls are built to kill many people.
notes: Heb “deal with” or “work with.”

verses.zh: 他轻看誓言，背弃盟约，已经投降，却又做这一切的事，他必不能逃脱。」
verses.en: He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Take note[NOTE:1]—he gave his promise[NOTE:2] and did all these things. He will not escape!
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates being aware of or taking notice of something.
Heb “hand.” “Giving one’s hand” is a gesture of promise (2 Kgs 10:15).

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：「我指着我的永生起誓，他既轻看指我所起的誓，背弃指我所立的约，我必要使这罪归在他头上。
verses.en: “‘Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: As surely as I live, I will certainly repay him[NOTE:1] for despising my oath and breaking my covenant!
notes: Heb “place it on his head.”

verses.zh: 我必将我的网撒在他身上，他必在我的网罗中缠住。我必带他到巴比伦，并要在那里因他干犯我的罪刑罚他。
verses.en: I will throw my net over him and he will be caught in my snare; I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there because of the unfaithfulness he committed against me.

verses.zh: 他的一切军队，凡逃跑的，都必倒在刀下；所剩下的，也必分散四方（方：原文是风）。你们就知道说这话的是我―耶和华。」
verses.en: All the choice men[NOTE:1] among his troops will die[NOTE:2] by the sword, and the survivors will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken!
notes: Some manuscripts and versions read “choice men,” while most manuscripts read “fugitives”; the difference arises from the reversal, or metathesis, of two letters, מִבְרָחָיו (mivrakhayv) for מִבְחָריו (mivkharayv).
Heb “fall.”

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「我要将香柏树梢拧去栽上，就是从尽尖的嫩枝中折一嫩枝，栽于极高的山上；
verses.en: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: “‘I will take a sprig[NOTE:1] from the lofty top of the cedar and plant it.[NOTE:2] I will pluck from the top one of its tender twigs; I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
notes: The language is analogous to messianic imagery in Isa 11:1; Zech 3:8; 6:4, although the technical terminology is not the same.
The LXX lacks “and plant it.”

verses.zh: 在以色列高处的山栽上。它就生枝子，结果子，成为佳美的香柏树，各类飞鸟都必宿在其下，就是宿在枝子的荫下。
verses.en: I will plant it on a high mountain of Israel, and it will raise branches and produce fruit and become a beautiful cedar. Every bird will live under it; every winged creature will live in the shade of its branches.

verses.zh: 田野的树木都必知道我―耶和华使高树矮小，矮树高大；青树枯干，枯树发旺。我―耶和华如此说，也如此行了。」
verses.en: All the trees of the field will know that I am the Lord.I make the high tree low; I raise up the low tree. I make the green tree wither, and I make the dry tree sprout.I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will do it!’”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is a riddle/parable of

- Neo-Babylon, Nebuchaddnezzar II (605-562 B.C.) ‒ a great eagle, vv. 3-6,12

- Egypt, either Pharaoh Psammetichus II (Psamtik), who reigned from 593-588 or Pharaoh Apries (Hophea), who reigned from 588-569 ‒ another great eagle, vv. 7-8

- the vine, the Faith remnant ‒ a twig, a branch, vv. 22-24

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

- The historical context is Nebuchadnezzar II's exile of Josiah's son, Jehoiachin and the appointment of
Josiah's third son, Zedekiah, as vassal king. In turn, Zedekiah approached Egypt for a military alliance (cf. 2 Kgs. 24-28;
2 Chr. 36; Jer. 52). As a result, Neo-Babylon's army invaded again.

- There is a future hope in

- Cyrus II's victory over Neo-Babylon (notice Isa. 44:45; 45:1). Persia let all captured national people groups return home.
Mostly, Judah returned to a small province surrounding Jerusalem under Zerubbable and Joshua.

- There are clear hints in the text that this passage may have an ultimate fulfillment in Jesus, the true Davidic Messiah (cf. Isa. 11; Jer. 23:5-6)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 17:1-6

1Now the word of the Lord came to me saying, 2"Son of man,
propound a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel, 3saying, 'Thus says the Lord God, "A great eagle with great wings,
long pinions and a full plumage of many colors came to Lebanon and took away the top of the cedar. 4He plucked off the topmost of its young twigs and brought
it to a land of merchants; he set it in a city of traders. 5He also took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil. He placed it beside abundant
waters; he set it like a willow. 6Then it sprouted and became a low, spreading vine with its branches turned toward him, but its roots remained under it. So it
became a vine and yielded shoots and sent out branches."

17:2 This verse has two parallel IMPERATIVES.

- "propound a riddle," BDB 295, KB 309, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Jdg. 14:12-19

- "speak a parable," BDB 605 II, KB 648 I, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Ezek. 12:23;
16:44; 17:2; 18:2; 20:49; 24:3

The term "riddle" (BDB 295, note the relation of the VERB, BDB 295, and NOUN, BDB 295) means a
statement that needs to have some information hinted at or supplied to be understood (cf. Prov. 1:6).

The term "parable" (BDB 605 II, note the relation of the VERB, BDB 605 II, and NOUN,
BDB 605 II) implies a brief poetic structure, possibly a proverb which uses comparison as a way to illustrate truth. Ezekiel often used well known cultural proverbs.

Ezekiel has been using highly figurative language to convince the exiles of the just and sure judgment of Jerusalem.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERPRETING PARABLES

17:3 "a great eagle" The imaginary bird (eagle or vulture, a large bird of prey) is described as

- "great," BDB 152

- "great wings," BDB 152 CONSTRUCT BDB 489

- "long pinions," BDB 74 CONSTRUCT BDB 7

- "rich in plumage," BDB 570 CONSTRUCT BDB 663

- "of many colors," BDB 955

This is a description of the large mercenary and conscripted army of Neo-Babylon who captured Jerusalem
in 605, 597, 586, 582 B.C. In this context it is the 597 B.C. exile (i.e. "took
the top of the cedar") in which Ezekiel and thousands of other craftsmen and leaders were taken to Babylon
(cf. Ezek. 17:12-13; 2 Kgs. 24:24,15).

▣ "Lebanon" This is imagery referring to Judah. Possibly

- It is used because the parable will involve tall cedars and Lebanon was famous for hers (cf. Ezek. 31:3).

- Solomon's palace was paneled and beamed with cedars from Lebanon (cf. 1 Kgs. 7:1-3). The remodeled palace
was called "The House of the Forest of Lebanon" (cf. 1 Kgs. 7:2; 10:17,21; 2 Chr. 9:16).

▣

NASB, NRSV, JPSOA, TEV, NJB, NET
"top"

NKJV
"the highest branch"

REB
"the very top"

Peshitta
"the choicest branch"

LXX
"the choice branches"

This term (BDB 856, KB 1035) is found only in Ezekiel (i.e. Ezek. 17:3,22; 31:3,10,14). Its
etymology is unknown. The meaning is derived from the context.

- Neo-Babylon ‒ Ezek. 17:3

- Messianic ‒ Ezek. 17:22 (cf. Isa. 11)

SPECIAL TOPIC: BRANCH OF THE LORD

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE

- Assyria ‒ Ezek. 31:3,10

17:4 The destination of exiled Judean society is described as

- "to a land of trade," BDB 488 II (e.g. Ezek. 16:15-20)

- "a city of traders," BDB 746, and BDB 940, KB 1237, Qal PARTICIPLE

Back in Ezek. 12:13 Chaldea is the resettled destination of the Judean exiles (cf. Ezek. 1:3). The term "Chaldea"
(BDB 505) may be related to the term "Canaanite" (BDB 489, or "merchants" in Ezek. 16:29, where they appear together).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

17:5 This is a description of the relatively easy treatment of the first exiles. They were settled by a canal and given limited autonomy.

17:5 "land" The MT has "the seed of the land." This would refer to the exiled Davidic seed, Jehoiachin (v. 12, cf. Ezek. 1:2).
But the JPSOA, in a footnote, suggests an emendation to "cedar."

- land, ארץ (BDB 75)

- cedar, ארז (BDB 72)

Both make sense in this context and refer to transplanted and restored Judean captives (esp. their Davidic leader).

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"placed it beside abundant waters"

NRSV, LXX
"a plant by abundant waters"

REB
"a shoot beside abundant waters"

NJB
"by the side of a generous stream"

JPSOA
"planted it. . .beside abundant waters"

The problem is the Hebrew CONSONANTS (word), קח (BDB 881 brief note), which does not
exist. Therefore, most translations supply the VERB "place" or "set" (BDB 542, KB 534,
Qal IMPERFECT with waw,
לקח).

NASB, REB, JPSOA, NET
"like a willow"

NKJV, NJB
"like a willow tree"

NRSV
"like a willow twig"

TEV
"young plant"

This term (BDB 861) is found only here in the OT. It seems to be of onomatopoeic origin from the
Arabic term for "rustling." Context implies an easily germinating tree twig (cf. Ezek. 17:22).

The two ancient translations translate this last line differently.

- LXX ‒ "he set it in a conspicuous place"

- Peshitta ‒ "and set a watchman over it"

17:6 This verse describes the low growth of the remaining Judeans in Judea. They were still in the Promised
Land, but were very weak as a vassal nation (cf. Ezek. 17:13-14).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 17:7-10

7"But there was another great eagle with great wings and much
plumage; and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him and sent out its branches toward him from the beds where it was planted, that he might water it.
8It was planted in good soil beside abundant waters, that it might yield branches and bear fruit and become a splendid vine." 9Say,
'Thus says the Lord God, "Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and cut off its fruit, so that it withers-so that all its sprouting
leaves wither? And neither by great strength nor by many people can it be raised from its roots again. 10Behold, though it is planted, will it thrive?
Will it not completely wither as soon as the east wind strikes it - wither on the beds where it grew?"'"

17:7 "another eagle" The first eagle referred to Nebuchadnezzar II. This refers to Egypt (cf. Ezek. 17:15). Judah looked to
Egypt for military aid and protection (i.e. Jeremiah 37).

The MT has "one" but the LXX has "another." This is another example of Hebrew CONSONANTS "R"
and "D" being confused.

- "one" ‒ אחד (MT)

- "another" ‒ אחר (LXX, JPSOA, Peshitta)

The UBS Text Project, p. 49, mentions that this same "d" ‒ "r" confusion occurs in Ezek. 11:19; 19:5; 34:23; 37:16.

17:8 There is a series of Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS. They describe in this verse (1) how King Zedekiah
believed that an alliance with Egypt would help Judah or (2) a repeat of Ezek. 17:5, illustrating that there was no need for Zedekiah to rebel and seek help from Egypt

- that it might yield branches

- that it might bear fruit

- that it might become a splendid vine

17:9-10 These are parallel and describe Judah's attempt to seek help from Egypt, but YHWH will not
allow it.

17:9 "leaves" This term (BDB 383) normally refers to the prey of a lion, killed and torn apart
(cf. Ezek. 19:3,6; 22:25,27). Only here does it refer to plucked leaves (although the same CONSONANTS with
different VOWELS refer to plucked olive leaves in Gen. 8:11).

17:10 "completely wither" This is an emphatic grammatical construction that uses
the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and the IMPERFECT VERB
of the same root (BDB 386, KB 384) together. The VERB is used twice in
Ezek. 17:9 and twice in Ezek. 17:10.

▣ "the east wind" This CONSTRUCT (BDB 924 and BDB 870) is used as
an active representation of God's power (ruah) to accomplish His purposes. The east wind is
associated with judgments and the west wind with blessings.

- the Lord directed an east wind. . .brought the locusts, Exod. 13:10

- the Lord swept the sea back by a strong east wind, Exod. 14:21; 15:10

- with the east wind, Thou does break the ships of Tarshish, Ps. 48:7

- like an east wind I will scatter them (Israel) before the enemy, Jer. 18:17

- completely wither as soon as the east wind strikes it (Judah), Ezek. 17:10

- the east wind dried up its (Israel) fruit, Ezek. 19:12

- the east wind has broken you (Tyre), Ezek. 27:26

- an east wind will come. . .his (Israel) spring will be dried up, Hosea 13:15

- God appointed a scorching east wind, Jonah 4:8

- an east wind is implied in Job 1:19 and Jer. 4:11

The west wind is mentioned once in Exod. 10:19 and implied in Num. 11:31. Rain would come from
a northwesterly direction.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 17:11-21

11Moreover, the word of the Lord
came to me, saying, 12"Say now to the rebellious house, 'Do you not know what these things mean?' Say, 'Behold, the king of Babylon
came to Jerusalem, took its king and princes and brought them to him in Babylon. 13He took one of the royal family and made a covenant with him,
putting him under oath. He also took away the mighty of the land, 14that the kingdom might be in subjection, not exalting itself, but keeping his
covenant that it might continue. 15But he rebelled against him by sending his envoys to Egypt that they might give him horses and many troops. Will
he succeed? Will he who does such things escape? Can he indeed break the covenant and escape? 16As I live,' declares the Lord
God, 'Surely in the country of the king who put him on the throne, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, in Babylon
he shall die. 17Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company will not help him in the war, when they cast up ramps and build siege walls to
cut off many lives. 18Now he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, and behold, he pledged his allegiance, yet did all these things; he shall not
escape.'" 19Therefore, thus says the Lord God, "As I live, surely My oath which he despised and My covenant which he broke,
I will inflict on his head. 20I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare. Then I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him
there regarding the unfaithful act which he has committed against Me. 21All the choice men in all his troops will fall by the sword, and the survivors will
be scattered to every wind; and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken."

17:11-21 This is the interpretation of the imagery of Ezek. 17:1-10 about the two great eagles.

17:11-12 "saying, Say. . ." This is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 55, KB 65),
repeated for emphasis. YHWH is speaking to Judah through His prophet.

17:12 "the rebellious house" This is a characteristic phrase of Ezekiel referring to Judah (cf. Ezek. 2:5,6,8;
3:9,26,27; 12:2 [twice],3,9,25; 17:12; 24:3). Moses first called the covenant people rebellious (BDB 598) in Deut. 9:7; 31:27.

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

▣ "the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and princes, and brought them to him in
Babylon" This exile is recorded in 2 Kings 24. The date would be 597 B.C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF NEO-BABYLON

17:13 The new Neo-Babylonian puppet king was Jehoiachin's uncle, Mattaniah, whose name was changed to Zedekiah
(cf. 2 Kgs. 24:17; 2 Chr. 36:10). He made a loyalty oath to Neo-Babylon (v. 16), which he later broke seeking help from Egypt (v. 15).

17:14 Nebuchadnezzar II was hoping that the partial deportation would teach Judah a lesson and keep them
a vassal nation (i.e. paying tribute, cf. Jeremiah 27), but it did not work (cf. Ezek. 17:16).

17:15 "But he rebelled" See 2 Kgs. 24:20, where Zedekiah, King of Judah, rebelled

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 17:22-24

22Thus says the Lord God, "I will also take a sprig from
the lofty top of the cedar and set it out; I will pluck from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
23On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, that it may bring forth boughs and bear fruit and become a stately cedar. And birds of every kind will
nest under it; they will nest in the shade of its branches. 24All the trees of the field will know that I am the Lord; I bring
down the high tree, exalt the low tree, dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I am the Lord; I have spoken, and I will perform it."

17:22-23 Again, at the end of a judgment oracle there is hope for a future for YHWH's covenant
people (cf. Ezek. 16:60-63).

17:22 "young twigs a tender one" The imagery of a newly planted twig begins in vv. 1-6, referring to Judah in exile. However,
here the imagery is repeated of a future national hope in Canaan. This hope is a returning Davidic seed.

The concept of a "shoot," "stem," or "branch" (cf. Isa. 11:1) becomes a Messianic symbol of the restoration of the Davidic
seed (cf. 2 Samuel 9; Psalm 89).

The Branch (cf. Isa. 4:2; 11:1; 53:2; Jer. 23:5; 33:15; Zech. 3:8; 6:12; Acts 13:23; Rom. 15:12) becomes the hope of all
mankind for YHWH to fulfill His promises to Israel and to the nations! Remember Gen. 3:15 is a promise to humanity made in YHWH's image, not Israel!

17:23 "birds of every kind" This is a universal element (i.e. ANE's "cosmic tree"), as is the phrase, "all the trees of the field" in Ezek. 17:24.
Isaiah captures this same planting imagery that reaches all the world in Isa. 27:6. YHWH has an eternal redemptive plan for all the sons and daughters of Adam, not just Jacob's children!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

17:24 YHWH describes His control of His creation in a series of plant imagery.

- I bring down the high tree

- I exalt the low tree (i.e. here)

- I dry up the green tree

- I make the dry tree flourish

Examples of #1,3 would be Egypt in Ezekiel 31 and Neo-Babylon in Daniel 4. An example of #2,4 would be the
promises to restore Israel/Judah (Ezek. 16:60-63; 17:24). In the NT the mustard seed and resulting large bush become the symbol of a
universal cosmic tree (cf. Matt. 13:31-32; Mark 4:30-32; Luke 13:18-19. Also note Dan. 4:12,21), which is the kingdom of our God and His Christ!

The final statement, "I am the Lord; I have spoken, and I will perform it," is a key theological
statement (i.e. Isa. 55:9-11). Humans can depend on God's word, both His judgments and His promises! He is the creator and controller of all life!
History/time are in His hands (cf. Ezek. 12:25,28; 22:14; Isa. 14:24; 55:11)!
